significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an early harmfulness signal "decays roughly monotonically with the number of CoT tokens" across benign and adversarial reasoning until it crosses a refusal threshold, while restoring the cached early signal causally restores refusal; this combines a form-(iii) predictive decay law with a form-(ii) intervention. Unlike the topic-median direction-and-steering hypothesis exemplified by Arditi et al.'s "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction," the proposed law fixes expected signal trajectories and compliance risk at untested reasoning lengths and offers both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic explanation. A negative result would informatively rule out content-independent length dilution as the common explanation for the three named failure regimes, although it would leave content-specific mechanisms unresolved; verified true and false are therefore distinguishable. In the topic-substitution check, deleting the decay law and cached-verdict mechanism leaves only generic mechanistic LLM safety, which would not earn this score, so the rating comes from the claim-specific predictive coupling rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The named handle is "Self-Verdict Anchoring (SVA)," operationally described as "a per-token projection plus a boundary nudge" that caches the model's early verdict and re-injects it before generation of the final answer. It is ex ante relative to harmful output and gives model labs an action window at inference time, although activation access confines direct uptake mainly to developers or deployers of instrumentable reasoning models. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed monotone length-to-signal/refusal relation still predicts what should occur at new lengths and under multiple reasoning regimes, while the exact direction and anchor strength require recalibration; the asserted scope spans reasoning LLMs and several classes of length-based attacks rather than one dataset. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this reach score: generic safety interpretability supplies neither this forward-looking quantity nor the boundary intervention, so the score rests on the transferable relation and usable defense.
